text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Investors on the Oslo stock exchange are becoming more nervous after four years of steady gains on the bourse. Analyst Guttorm Egge says investors might be wise to put their money under the matress for a while.
-State-owned oil company Statoil has bought a 14.5 percent interest in Swedish natural gas company Vattenfall Naturgas AB. Statoil paid nearly 100 million crowns for the stake.
-Fifteen doctors lost their licence to practise last year, which is two more than the total for 1994 and 1996 put together.
-Norway's hotel industry had a good year in 1996. Total revenues rose by 300 million crowns from 1995.
-A majority in parliament voted no to the Conservatives' suggestion to privatise state-owned telecommunications company Telenor.
